name: Facet-0
summary: General VLAs are trained on vision and do poorly when success depends on contact: insertions, snap-fits, connectors. Facet-0 makes force a first-class input and output. A reasoning VLM plans at 5-10 Hz while a precision controller runs at about 200 Hz; a force-residual head takes the wrist force/torque history and corrects coarse action-and-force chunks in a closed loop at about 20 Hz, and a safety critic scores candidate actions and blocks ones that would exceed contact-safe force bounds. Training runs in three stages: pretraining on ManuFacet-1K (about 1,000 hours of force-synchronised teleoperated precision-assembly data) plus assembly VQA, post-training with reward-driven updates from real-world rollouts, and few-shot, safety-bounded adaptation that updates about 6.6% of the weights. On five precision computer-assembly tasks the task-adapted system averaged 82% success versus 15% for the strongest baseline, at 0.5 mm action precision.
innovation: Predicts action and force chunks together and corrects them from measured wrench, instead of treating force as an afterthought to vision.
A learned safety critic gates execution, so real-world RL can run on contact-rich tasks without damaging parts.
matters: Targets the industrial tasks (electronics assembly) where vision-only VLAs fail, with a large margin over baselines.
Code and data give other labs a starting point for force-aware foundation models.
limits: Evaluated on one domain (computer assembly) with a single sensor setup.
Requires a wrist F/T sensor, which many low-cost arms lack.
lineage: Hierarchical VLM-plus-controller design in the line of Hi Robot, with RL from real rollouts as in pi-0.6 RECAP, adding force as a predicted modality.
